description:
Found 2026-09-14 while verifying op-u9jp. NOT caused by that change -- identical under both the old (bg_1 + resonance total) and new (sum of parts) MT=1 constructions, so it predates both.

On U-234 (ENDF/B-VIII.0, MAT 9225) reconstructed at err=0.001, sweeping NJOY's own grid below 20 keV, the worst relative deviation on MT=1 is 1.0000e0 at E=1.70000e3 eV: ours 0.000000e0 against NJOY 2.032567e1 b. A relative deviation of exactly 1.0 with ours at zero means our MF=3 MT=1 section has no coverage at that energy at all, not that the value is wrong -- eval_lin_lin returns 0.0 outside a section's tabulated range.

Hypothesis, NOT verified: the reconstruction grid does not span the full evaluation range for this material, so energies between the resolved-range top and wherever the background resumes fall into a hole. U-234 has a (1,2)+(2,2) LRU/LRF structure -- both a resolved and an unresolved range -- so the boundary between them is the obvious place to look.

Consequence if real: any consumer evaluating the total cross section in that window gets 0.0, which in transport means an infinite flight. U-234 is one of Godiva's three ICSBEP nuclides, though at 4.9184e-4 /b*cm and a fast spectrum the practical exposure may be small. Not assessed.

Reproduce: reconr(n-092_U_234-ENDF8.0.endf, mat 9225, err 0.001) and evaluate MtReaction::Mt1Total at 1700 eV; compare with an NJOY2016 RECONR run using the committed deck reference-data/reconr/u234-ENDF8.0-0K-err0.001.njoy-input.

Check the other partials and the other materials at the same boundary before assuming it is U-234-specific -- only MT=1 was swept here.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-14 ROOT-CAUSED. This is NOT a grid gap as the title says -- RETITLE SUGGESTED to: 'reconr: unresolved-range cross sections are never reconstructed into MF=3; LSSF=0 materials come back at ZERO'.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG: reconr parses LRU=2 (unresolved) ranges as HEADER ONLY and never reconstructs them. reconr/mf2.rs::parse_lru2_header carried the comment 'RECONR does not use unresolved parameters (that is PURR's job)', which is WRONG ABOUT UPSTREAM. reconr.f90's own header (:81-87) says the opposite: 'If unresolved parameters are present, the infinitely dilute cross sections are computed on a special energy grid ... and the table is also used to compute the unresolved contributions in MF3.' PURR owns the SELF-SHIELDED treatment; the INFINITELY DILUTE one belongs in RECONR. reconr/mod.rs:17 already called this 'next to port ... blocks sigma above the resolved region', so it was a known gap that a second, mistaken comment made look intentional.

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS LSSF, AND IT IS WHY THIS HID. Measured:
  U-234 (MAT 9225)  URR [1.500e3, 1.000e5]  LSSF=0  -> 7/10 log-spaced MT=1 samples are 0.0
  U-235 (MAT 9228)  URR [2.250e3, 2.500e4]  LSSF=1  -> 0/10 zero
  U-238 (MAT 9237)  URR [2.000e4, 1.490e5]  LSSF=1  -> 0/10 zero
With LSSF=1 the evaluation's MF=3 ALREADY carries the infinitely-dilute unresolved cross sections, so adding nothing is correct. With LSSF=0 it does not, and the window is left empty. Every case this repo runs is built on U-235/U-238, both LSSF=1, so the defect is invisible on them. (Same flag as the U-238 lesson recorded in the workspace CLAUDE.md 'read upstream first' section -- this is its mirror image.)

SEVERITY: at 1700 eV ours is 0.000000e0 against NJOY 2.032567e1 b. MT=2, MT=18 and MT=102 are zero across the window too, and the MF=3 background is itself zero, so nothing fills it. A ZERO TOTAL CROSS SECTION IS AN INFINITE FLIGHT IN TRANSPORT. U-234 is one of Godiva's three ICSBEP nuclides (4.9184e-4 /b*cm, fast spectrum, so practical exposure there is probably small -- NOT assessed).

THIS IS WIRING, NOT PORTING -- the machinery exists. unresr::unresolved_cross_sections (src/unresr/, ~72 KB across mf2.rs/mod.rs/wfun.rs, ported and with U-235/U-238 golden tests) computes exactly what is needed; pass sig0=[1e10] for infinite dilution and sigbkg zeroed when LSSF>0, per its own doc. It is currently consumed ONLY by PURR. Note unresr::mf2::parse_lru2_ranges takes the section rows from the PER-ISOTOPE CONT, i.e. &sec.rows[1..] -- calling it with &sec.rows returns an empty vec silently, which cost a wrong measurement here before tests/purr_u235_urr.rs:41 showed the convention.

BLAST RADIUS IF FIXED: guard on lssf==0 and only LSSF=0 materials change. Among everything in reference-data/endf/ that is U-234 alone, so this can be landed and measured against a single NJOY oracle -- regenerable from the committed deck reference-data/reconr/u234-ENDF8.0-0K-err0.001.njoy-input (NJOY2016 ac5adf5f, gfortran 13.3.0; the 9 MB tape22 is not committed).

NOT ATTEMPTED. Reconstructing onto NJOY's 'special energy grid chosen to preserve the required interpolation properties', plus the MF=2/MT=152 table it also writes, is a real piece of work and doing it half-way would be worse than the honest hole. The false doc comment IS corrected in this pass so the next reader is not told the gap is intentional.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-14 UPSTREAM READ AND SIZED, so this is a specified task rather than a research one. Correcting one thing in my own earlier comment first: I wrote that unresr::unresolved_cross_sections is 'exactly what is needed'. That is the ETOX SELF-SHIELDED calculator (unresr.f90), and it is not what RECONR calls. RECONR has its OWN infinitely-dilute routines. Reusing the ETOX one at sig0=1e10 might reduce to the same numbers, but that is an assumption, not a fact, and it should be measured against the oracle rather than assumed.

WHAT RECONR ACTUALLY DOES (reconr.f90, upstream ac5adf5f):
  genunr   :1628-1735  (108 lines)  computes infinitely dilute XS on the eunr grid, lays it out in MF=2/MT=152 format, and -- the key branch -- 'if (lssf.ne.0) return' at :1694 before it adds the unresolved background from MF=3. This IS the LSSF discriminator, in upstream's own code.
  csunr1   :3826-4077  (252 lines)  Case A/B unresolved cross sections
  csunr2   :4079-4317  (239 lines)  Case C unresolved cross sections
  sigunr   :1737-1769  (33 lines)   retrieves from the genunr table during reconstruction; called at :2662
  total                 632 lines, plus the eunr grid construction scattered through rdf2u0/rdf2u1 (:1303, :1380-1400, :1510-1531) and the sigfig(el/eh,7,-+1) seam shading at :757-775, and the sort at :856-865.

GATING: genunr is called from :352 under 'if (lrp.eq.3)'. Check what LRP=3 means on the materials in hand before wiring -- I did not chase it, and getting the gate wrong would either skip materials that need it or run it on ones that do not.

SO THIS IS A ~630-LINE PORT plus grid construction, not the small wiring job my earlier comment implied. Retracting that estimate.

ORACLE IS READY: reference-data/reconr/u234-ENDF8.0-0K-err0.001.njoy-input regenerates NJOY2016's U-234 PENDF (9 MB, not committed). U-234 is LSSF=0 with URR [1.5e3, 1.0e5] and is the only LSSF=0 material in reference-data/endf/, so the blast radius of a fix is exactly one material and the gate is a single comparison. Target: MT=1 at 1700 eV should go from 0.000000e0 to NJOY's 2.032567e1 b.

ALSO WORTH CHECKING WHEN THIS IS DONE: genunr writes MF=2/MT=152. This crate does not emit that section at all as far as I saw, and PURR/UNRESR consumers may expect it. Not investigated.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-14 THE RESIDUAL IS EXPLAINED, AND THE ACCURACY CLAIM IS NOW EARNED BY EXPERIMENT RATHER THAN ASSERTED.

After wiring the URR reconstruction, total/elastic agreed with NJOY to ~5e-4 but fission/capture sat at 4-6e-3, which I first recorded as 'not understood'. It is now understood.

MECHANISM: of the 34 grid points NJOY writes in U-234's URR, 26 agree with our kernel to ~1e-7. The other 8 are each reproduced -- to between 2.9e-7 and 1.4e-16 -- by lin-lin interpolation of NJOY's OWN neighbouring exact points. That is genunr/sigunr working as documented: genunr (reconr.f90:1628-1735) tabulates the dilute cross sections on eunr as MF=2/MT=152, and sigunr (:1737-1769) INTERPOLATES that table for PENDF energies contributed by other MF=3 sections.

THREE EXPLANATIONS TESTED AND REJECTED FIRST: (a) a different ENDF interpolation law on the table -- no single law fits, log-lin was closest for MT=18 (3.7e-4) but lin-log for MT=102 (1.3e-3); (b) a difference in how the unresolved PARAMETERS are interpolated -- rejected by reading upstream, intr (unresr.f90:1261-1288) uses terp1 with int FORCED to 2 at :1057-1058, exactly as our interp_case_c does, so discarding the file's INT flag is correct; (c) parameter energies being privileged -- rejected by the data, 1.7e3/1e4/3e4/5e4 are not parameter energies and are exact while 7e3 is not one and is interpolated.

THE GAP I HAD TO CLOSE: agreement at nodes plus disagreement between them does NOT show which code is closer to the truth -- an implementation right at the nodes and wrong in between gives identical evidence. So I ran a refinement study that could falsify us.

DESIGN: NJOY forces the parameter interpolation law to lin-lin, so inserting lin-lin-interpolated parameter points is EXACT -- the physics is pointwise unchanged -- while eunr gets finer and RECONR evaluates where it previously interpolated. U-234's 10 parameter energies refined to 19/37/73/145; NJOY re-run on each.

CONTROL (this is what makes it interpretable): at every original parameter energy, at every refinement level, NJOY's output is BIT-IDENTICAL to baseline (0.00e+00). Across all 45,954 shared grid points the median and 95th-percentile difference are exactly zero.

RESULT -- NJOY converges onto our values:
  E          baseline    x16
  7.0e3      -9.00e-4    -3.33e-5
  4.368748e4 +5.80e-3    +1.90e-5
  4.518e4    +6.25e-3    +4.70e-5
  5.25e4     +3.70e-3    +4.29e-10
  7.0e4      -4.62e-3    +8.59e-8
  8.0e4      -5.69e-3    -1.86e-7
  9.0e4      -4.71e-3    -3.53e-7

Convergence is NOT monotone everywhere: 7.0e3 and 9.0e4 get worse at x2 before improving, because inserting points changes which neighbours bracket the target. Recorded rather than smoothed.

ONE SELF-CORRECTION ON THE RECORD: the Python comparison script reported several x16 entries as exactly 0.00e+00. They are not -- that was an artefact of rounding OUR values to the 7 figures NJOY prints. The Rust gate compares unrounded and resolves 4.29e-10 / 8.59e-8. The write-up quotes the weaker honest number (worst 4.7e-5) and explains the discrepancy.

DELIVERABLES: verification_and_validation/urr_interpolation_study/README.md (arXiv-format study: abstract, mechanism, baseline, rejected explanations, design, control, convergence, scope limits, reproduction, provenance) + the four scripts + the deck; tests/reconr_urr_njoy_converges_to_ours.rs (convergence gate + the control gate); both refined tapes committed at reference-data/reconr/u234-ENDF8.0-paramgrid-x16.endf and -0K-err0.001-paramgrid-x16.pendf.

SCOPE, stated in the paper: one material, one reaction, LSSF=0, infinite dilution, 0 K. Says nothing about NJOY's resolved-range reconstruction or its self-shielded URR path (UNRESR/PURR). Verification, not validation -- no measurement involved.

MAINTAINER DECISION NEEDED: the study scripts are Python, which this workspace's CLAUDE.md bars for documentation and accounting. This is neither -- a one-off ENDF-tape experiment -- and Python keeps the reproduction bar at 'run a script' rather than 'build a 40-crate Rust workspace', which matters if this is submitted. Flagged in the README's section 6 rather than decided unilaterally.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-15 MAINTAINER DECISIONS RECORDED, and the study is figure-complete.

1. PYTHON: 'Python for arXiv plotting is fine. That's one of the exceptions.' The flagged question is settled -- the study's scripts stand as written, and README section 6 now records the decision and its date rather than posing it as open. Noted there that the comparison arm itself is NOT Python: urr_kernel_dump is a Rust example, so the values NJOY is compared against never pass through a second implementation of the kernel.

2. PAPER SCOPE: 'Leave the paper scope narrow.' Unchanged -- one material, one reaction, LSSF=0, infinite dilution, 0 K. The section-5 limitations stay as written. Not broadening to a second LSSF=0 evaluation.

3. FOAM MERGE: closed by the maintainer ('good enough'). For the record, checked twice: claude/outram-foam-8ookor had 0 commits not already in develop, and no branch carried unmerged outram-foam changes.

ADDED THIS PASS:
- examples/urr_kernel_dump.rs -- dumps the kernel's MT=18 at full precision to ours_mt18.csv. Exists specifically so the analysis never compares against values rounded to NJOY's 7 printed figures.
- deviations.py -- computes the deviation table from the NJOY tapes plus that CSV, emitting deviations.csv.
- plot_convergence.py + fig1_convergence.{pdf,png} -- the convergence figure.

THE FULL-PRECISION TABLE REPLACES THE ROUNDED ONE, and it improves the story rather than papering over it. The entries previously shown as '~0' are 4.29e-10, 8.59e-8, -1.86e-7, -3.53e-7 -- and they are CONSTANT across refinement levels once reached, because they sit at the ~7e-7 quantisation of NJOY's own printed output. So four of seven series converge as far as the comparison can resolve and then stop; the other three fall by 27-300x and are still above the floor at x16 (worst 4.7e-5). More informative than 'exactly zero', and it is what the figure shows.

FIGURE DESIGN, for the record: the categorical palette was run through the validator rather than eyeballed. All hard checks pass; the contrast check WARNs on three slots against a white surface, which obligates visible direct labels -- so every series is labelled at its line end rather than carried by a legend box, and each also gets a distinct marker so the figure survives greyscale printing. The shaded band is NJOY's output resolution, drawn so a log axis reaching 4e-10 cannot imply precision the comparison does not have. First render put the band caption through three of the lines; moved to the one region of the band no series crosses.

Still open on this bead and NOT addressed: only Case C is exercised, so unresolved_grid's log-spaced fallback for Case A / energy-independent Case B remains unverified (no held evaluation reaches it), and MF=2/MT=152 is still not written.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-15 MF=2/MT=152 CLOSED -- read, written, wired into reconr(), and verified against NJOY2016. Commits 6c057d812 and 5ebf3440b (pushed as c30228477 after rebase).

WHAT WAS MISSING: genunr (reconr.f90:1628-1735) stores the infinitely-dilute unresolved cross sections as MF=2/MT=152, and sigunr (:1737-1769) interpolates that table to fill MF=3. This crate had the READER (groupr::urr_pendf, GROUPR's stounr feeder) but no writer, so its own RECONR output could not feed its own GROUPR.

NOW: reconr() emits the section. Against NJOY's own, on U-234: 27 energies matching EXACTLY, and per column -- elastic 1.00e-13, fission 1.00e-13, capture 1.00e-13, total 9.00e-7 (total carries the MF=3 MT=1 background, which NJOY itself rounds with sigfig(...,7,0) at :1719).

MT=152 ALSO SETTLED THE INTERPOLATION QUESTION DIRECTLY, replacing the inferential argument in the urr_interpolation_study. The stored energy list includes 7.2e3 and 7.2e4 but NOT 7.0e3 or 7.0e4 -- exactly the agree/disagree split. Classifying every MF=3 point in the URR against that list gives a PERFECT PARTITION: 26 agree-and-stored, 8 differ-and-not-stored, ZERO in either off-diagonal cell. Neither set hard-coded; both derived from the tapes at run time.

THREE THINGS I GOT WRONG FIRST, ALL CAUGHT BY WRITING THE CHECKS AS TESTS:
1. Bare kernel vs MT=152 failed on TOTAL only (5/27, up to 4.1e-2) while the partials passed 0/27. Not a defect: for LSSF=0, genunr's tail (:1694-1727) adds the evaluation's MF=3 background to each stored column. U-234 carries no MF=3 for MT=2/18/102 in that window, so only the total moved. With the background added as genunr adds it, all 108 values agree to 6.94e-7.
2. eunr is NOT the parameter energies. rdf2u2 (:1499-1533) fills gaps wider than wide=1.26 from a built-in 78-node grid egridu (:1239-1251). My first implementation gave 25 points vs 27 because it filtered the parameter list to < eh BEFORE reading the next energy, so the gap above the last in-range parameter never filled 7.2e4 and 8.5e4. Upstream reads enex unconditionally.
3. THE PHASE ORDERING. genunr reads MF=3 off the INPUT tape (:1698) -- pure background. Building the table from sections after Phase 2b feeds it the RESOLVED reconstruction as background; at 1.5e3 eV, the one energy the resolved and unresolved ranges share, that overstated total by 32 % and elastic by 36 %. Building before Phase 2b fixes it, and the call site carries that measurement so the phases cannot be quietly reordered.

Also asserted: column 5 repeats the TOTAL (sunr(l+5)=sunr(l+1), :1690), not transport -- this crate's kernel returns transport as its fifth output, so the obvious wiring is wrong and nothing else reads that column; and a material with no LRU=2 range emits no section, matching the  gate at :352 (checked on Si-30).

API: ReconrResult gains unresolved_table: Option<Vec<[f64;6]>>, 0 K by construction, carried through broaden_result unchanged because BROADR does not touch MF=2 (UNRESR/PURR later replace it with a temperature-dependent one). UnresolvedTable gains points() and n_reactions(). Nine construction sites updated across broadr/gaspr/heatr/photon.

SIX GATES: tests/reconr_mt152_vs_njoy2016.rs (2), tests/reconr_mt152_writer_vs_njoy2016.rs (4).

STILL OPEN ON THIS BEAD, unchanged: only Case C is exercised, so unresolved_grid's log-spaced fallback for Case A / energy-independent Case B remains unverified -- no held evaluation reaches it. And the LSSF=1 path in build_mt152 (early return before the background addition) is implemented but unexercised, U-234 being the only LSSF=0 material held and U-235/U-238 the LSSF=1 ones.

Verified: njoy 861 passed / 0 failed; workspace check clean; outram-mc-libs 276/1 with the one failure being the pre-existing GPU test (no GPU in this container), established by stashing rather than assumed.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-15 BOTH OPEN ITEMS CLOSED. Neither was blocked -- the 'no held evaluation reaches it' note on this bead was simply wrong, and screening the tapes (reference-data/endf/screen_endf_flags.py) refuted it in one command.

WHAT THE SCREEN FOUND. Fe-58 (ENDF/B-VIII.0 Beta4, MAT 2637) carries LRU=2, LRF=1, LFW=0, LSSF=1 over 3.5e5..3.0e6 eV -- Case A and LSSF=1 in one evaluation. U-238 (MAT 9237) carries Case C with LSSF=1 and L<=2, which isolates the early return from the grid change. Case B had no evaluation at all (Fe-58 is the ONLY LRU=2/LRF=1 range among every held tape, and it is LFW=0), so it got a synthetic tape instead -- see below.

ITEM 2, LSSF=1: CLOSED EXACTLY. U-238's 84 energies match and all 336 stored values agree to 1.00e-13 (same seven printed digits; the residual is the last bit of the decoded f64 -- I first wrote the gate as exact equality and that was too strong). A separate structural gate proves the MF=3 background really is skipped: build_mt152 with U-238's real background and with an empty one produce byte-identical tables, and the test asserts the background offered was non-vacuous (218 positive MF=3 MT=1 points across the URR).

ITEM 1, THE GRID: CLOSED, AND IT WAS WORSE THAN 'UNVERIFIED'. Reading rdf2u0 first showed Case A does not use a log fill at all -- it walks the built-in 78-node egridu from el to eh, taking the first node at or above E + E/100. The 40-point log-spaced fallback was the WRONG GRID, not merely an unchecked one: 42 energies against NJOY's 13. Two more divergences fell out of reading the three rdf2u* side by side: the gap-fill step is E+E/100 in rdf2u0/rdf2u1 but E+E/1000 in rdf2u2; and Case C seeds from the first J-state of the first L-state alone (if (n.eq.1.and.l.eq.1), :1497), not the union I was taking -- the union agrees on U-234 because every J there tabulates the same mesh, which is why it went unnoticed.

ALSO FIXED, FOUND THE SAME WAY: intunr defaults to 5 (log-log, rdfil2:809) and is overridden only by Case C (rdf2u2:1487). It had been hard-coded to 2 -- U-234's value and no one else's. U-238 and Fe-58 both store 5. JStateC was discarding the INT field entirely; it now carries it.

CASE B GOT A SYNTHETIC ORACLE rather than being left open. reference-data/endf/synthetic-caseb-lfw1.generator.py builds a minimal format-legal LRU=2/LRF=1/LFW=1 tape that NJOY2016 processes without diagnostics, so RECONR's own output is still the reference -- same technique as the existing photoat-synthetic-Z6.endf. Parameters are invented and carry no physical claim; they are chosen for branch coverage: one fission-grid gap above wide=1.26 so the fill must fire and one below so it must not, the last grid energy exactly at EH so upstream's unguarded enex read never runs off the list, L<=1 to stay clear of op-33g1, and LSSF=0 so the background addition is exercised too. Result: 16 energies exactly, LSSF and intunr exact, all 64 stored values to 4.22e-7 (the seven-figure floor once the background is added, same as U-234's 9.00e-7).

A REAL UPSTREAM DEFECT CAME OUT OF THE FE-58 LEG -- filed as op-33g1. RECONR's unfac (reconr.f90:4473-4496) has no l>=3 branch, so vl and ps keep their previous values, and csunr1's vl = vl*e2 (:4010) sits inside the J loop, multiplying vl by another sqrt(E) per J-state. Fe-58 has NLS=4. NJOY's stored total therefore runs 1.42e4 b at 350 keV to 6.62e5 b at 3 MeV -- about 1900x the unitarity limit and RISING with energy, which no cross section does. Ours reads 4.57 and 4.76 b, tracking the evaluation's own MF=3. The test reproduces NJOY's numbers from the defective recurrence to 2.68e-7, so this is a measurement, not an opinion. NJOY's UNRESR does not share it: uunfac (unresr.f90:1213-1239) writes a bare else where unfac and PURR's unfac2 write 'else if (l.eq.2)', and this crate's kernel ports uunfac. A guard test pins the clamp so nobody 'fixes' it toward RECONR.

SEVEN GATES in tests/reconr_mt152_all_unresolved_cases_vs_njoy2016.rs (grid+flags over all three cases, U-238 values, Case B values, the no-background structural check, the penetrability clamp, and the fall-through reproduction). Oracles hold only the MF=2/MT=152 section -- U-238's full PENDF is 97 MB -- with decks and the extraction recorded in reference-data/reconr/README.md.

NOTHING LEFT OPEN ON THIS BEAD.

title: njoy reconr: U-234 MT=1 reads 0.0 at 1700 eV where NJOY gives 20.3 b -- reconstruction grid gap

description:
In steady state, flows are specified. In dynamic mode, flows must be SOLVED from the pressure field, otherwise a valve closing changes nothing downstream and the simulator is not really transient.

SCOPE: a simultaneous pressure-flow network over the flowsheet graph, with the resistance of valves and pipes and the head of pumps and compressors, so that flow rate becomes a computed variable driven by pressure differences and inventory changes. This is what couples a valve stroke to a downstream response.

Relates to op-1z3o.5 (the steady-state sequential-modular solver) but is a different mathematical problem — simultaneous rather than sequential — so it deserves its own solve path.

Reference DWSIM dynamic mode for the formulation. Enum dispatch over element types, no trait objects.
title: refinery: pressure-flow network solve for dynamic mode

description:
Goal: model the HTR-10 fuel pebble on the Li, Yu & Wei (2014) HTR 2014 Weihai Table 2 spec and solve it with exact delta (Woodcock) tracking.

LANDED
- TrisoSpec::HTR10_LI2014 (crates/outram-mc-libs/src/pebble_beds/fhr_pebble.rs)
  250 um kernel radius + 90/40/35/40 um buffer/IPyC/SiC/OPyC -> 455 um particle.
  packing_fraction 0.050247 is DERIVED (8335 particles in a 2.5 cm fuel zone), not quoted.
- PebbleParams::htr10_li2014() (crates/outram-mc-libs/src/dh_universe.rs)
  6 cm ball, 0.5 cm fuel-free shell, reflective at the pebble surface, no coolant.
- examples/htr10_pebble_delta_tracking.rs -- 7-material table from Table 2, ENDF/B-VIII.0
  + crystalline-graphite S(a,b) at 300.15 K (paper: "all materials at 27 C"),
  DhTreatment::DeltaTracking, plus a four-arm boron sensitivity study.

DISCREPANCY FOUND, NOT RESOLVED
geometry::TrisoRadii::HTR10 carries a 95 um buffer (460 um particle, 5.19 % packing);
Table 2 gives 90 um (455 um, 5.025 %). That is +3.3 % particle volume and packing.
The existing preset documents itself as "typical / reference values ... NOT an
authoritative specification". NEITHER has been checked against IAEA-TECDOC-1382, which
is the HTR-10 benchmark authority and IS already in crates/kovan-literature. Do not
silently unify them; adjudicate against the TECDOC first.

THREE AMBIGUITIES IN TABLE 2, all assumed and documented in the example module docs:
1. "Fuel enrichment 17%" -- no basis given. Taken as WEIGHT percent -> 17.1801 at%.
   The 5 g heavy-metal closure CANNOT arbitrate (4.99991 vs 4.99992 g) but the two
   readings differ by 1.06 % in U-235 number density.
2. No density for the fuel ball graphite; only the moderator ball (1.73 g/cm3) is given.
   Matrix and shell both assumed 1.73.
3. "ppm" -- no basis. Taken as by weight, of NATURAL boron (18.43 wt% B-10).

Hand estimate at 2200 m/s that motivated the sensitivity arms: boron is ~0.06 % of
kernel absorption but ~24 % of graphite absorption. Reading ppm as elemental B-10
over-absorbs by 5.43x.

NOT CLAIMED: this is a bare-pebble k-infinity. It is NOT comparable to the paper
Tables 3/4, which are whole-core k-eff vs loading height. No published reference
k-inf was read, so none is asserted.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
MEASURED 2026-09-16, delta tracking, ENDF/B-VIII.0 + crystalline-graphite S(a,b) @ 300.15 K,
6000 histories x [20 inactive + 60 active]:

  arm                          k_inf      sigma    vs natural
  natural B (as specified)    1.68515   0.00178    (reference)
  no boron at all             1.70002   0.00175    +1487 pcm (6.0 sigma)
  graphite boron only         1.68297   0.00175     -218 pcm (0.9 sigma)
  ppm read as elemental B-10  1.62804   0.00191    -5711 pcm (21.9 sigma)

THE PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION HELD. Before running, a 2200 m/s hand estimate put the
kernel 4 ppm at ~0.06 % of local absorption and the graphite 1.3 ppm at ~24 %, so dropping
the kernel boron was predicted to be invisible. It is: 0.9 sigma, with a negative sign that
cannot be physical (removing an absorber cannot lower k), i.e. noise.

So essentially ALL of the +1487 pcm is the graphite 1.3 ppm. And misreading that one row as
elemental B-10 costs 5711 pcm -- almost 4x the impurity own worth, because it multiplies
the absorber by 5.43x.

CROSS-RUN AGREEMENT: an earlier 2000-history run gave natural 1.68532 +/- 0.00308, 17 pcm
away, with +1093 (2.7s) / -536 (1.2s) / -5974 (14.3s). Every arm consistent; both
unresolved nulls STAYED unresolved as statistics improved rather than resolving into
something, which is the right behaviour for a genuine null.

Results are recorded in the example module docs per the V&V rule. The composition now lives
in pebble_beds::htr10 (e31de690c) with 7 tests, including an atom-density regression
against figures computed by hand OUTSIDE the crate -- that is what lets these numbers stay
quotable across the refactor that moved the arithmetic into the library.

THE PROBLEM. IAEA-TECDOC-1382 part 2 (OPEN tier, crates/kovan-literature/generated/markdown/open/iaea-tecdoc-1382-part2.md) line 189 is a bare caption, 'FIG. 4.10. HTR-10 core physics calculation model (see Table 4-3)'. Table 4-3 (lines 179-187) gives ONLY zone number -> carbon atom density -> natural boron atom density -> a one-line remark, for 83 zones. Core radius, conus angle, discharge-tube radius, cavity height and the axial coordinates of every zone boundary are ABSENT AS TEXT. The formal B1 definition subsection (4.1.2.1) is also missing from the markdown conversion - its body was absorbed into the Table 4-3 dump, gap at lines 170-198.

WHAT IS TEXTUALLY AVAILABLE (use, but it is not enough):
- Core radius 90 cm (line 1453); core diameter 180 cm (line 43); mean height 197 cm.
- Russia's FIG 4.20 axis labels survive as bare OCR'd numbers (lines 775-801): radial 90, 95.6, 108.6, 167.793, 190; axial 105, 114.7, 130, 171.698, 351.818, 388.764, 402, 430. KEY statement at line 799: Z = 351.818 cm corresponds to zero core height, i.e. the top of the conus. The pairing of these numbers to specific zone boundaries is NOT recoverable and must not be treated as authoritative.
- Control-rod channel 13 cm diameter at r = 102.1 cm; rod lower end 119.2 cm withdrawn, 394.2 cm inserted (lines 109, 111). Twenty helium channels 80 mm at r = 1446 mm, z = 1050-6100 mm (line 197).
- VTB's Griffin deck gives an outer bound: vacuum at sqrt(x^2+y^2) > 165.0, bottom z < 41, top z > 490 (reference-data/virtual_test_bed/htgr/htr10/steady/htr-10-critical.i:74, :80-81, :88-89).

THREE ROUTES, MAINTAINER TO CHOOSE:
1. Read the dimensions off Figure 4.10 in the PDF (crates/kovan-literature/open/reports/iaea-tecdoc-1382-part2.pdf) and record the digitisation as a documented processing step per DATA_POLICY.md.
2. Obtain Terry, W.K. (2005), 'Evaluation of the initial critical configuration of the HTR-10 pebble-bed reactor', INL/CON-05-00852 - the geometry source Choo and Xiao (2024) cite.
3. Obtain the VTB HTR-10 mesh from upstream, which encodes the geometry directly. NOTE it is NOT in this checkout - see the VTB correction bead.

USEFUL AND ALREADY PRESENT: Table 4-3's 83-zone homogenised atom densities (lines 179-187), Table 4-37's pebble-bed cell geometry (line 1089), and Table 4-38's explicit atom densities (line 1101) which the rung-1 example already consumes.

notes.author: fifad@Teddy-Thinkpad
notes.content:
MAINTAINER DECISION 2026-08-13: route 2 chosen -- obtain Terry, W.K. (2005), 'Evaluation of the initial critical configuration of the HTR-10 pebble-bed reactor', INL/CON-05-00852. Rationale: an authoritative text source with real numbers beats digitising a figure, and procurement runs in parallel with the cfmesh meshing work so it costs no critical-path time.

FALLBACK, only if it cannot be obtained: route 1, digitise FIG 4.10 from crates/kovan-literature/open/reports/iaea-tecdoc-1382-part2.pdf using kovan-digitise. If it comes to that: use the CLI (never read points off the figure by eye -- CLAUDE.md hard rule), supply axis references explicitly since there is no tick-label OCR, and note that an agent run can ONLY ever emit Unreviewed -- the maintainer marks it reviewed.

ON ARRIVAL: catalogue Terry 2005 into kovan-literature with its access tier decided from its own copyright page, per the 'ANY literature ingested OR USED goes into kovan' hard rule. Check the extracted metadata round-trips through 'kovan lit bibtex' before trusting it.

notes.author: fifad@Teddy-Thinkpad
notes.content:
PARTIALLY RESOLVED 2026-08-13. The maintainer supplied Terry et al. (2005), INL/CON-05-00852, obtained from https://www.osti.gov/servlets/purl/911178. Catalogued as PROPRIETARY (its first page says 'should not be cited or reproduced without permission of the author' -- OSTI hosting grants no redistribution rights, and the tier comes from the copyright page per DATA_POLICY.md). PDF at crates/kovan-literature/proprietary/reports/terry2005-htr10-benchmark-evaluation.pdf (gitignored).

DIMENSIONS RECORDED, with provenance, in docs/reactor-scoping/htr10-neutronics.md, new final section. Its Table 2 supplies the axial build this bead said was absent from the open text:
  Height of core cavity  221.818 cm
  Height of conus         36.946 cm
  Core radius 90 cm, loading height 123.06 cm
  Reflector OD 380 cm, height 610 cm
  Discharge tube r = 25 cm, height 610 cm
  Cold coolant channels 8.0 cm dia at r = 144.6 cm, height 405 cm
  Control-rod/irradiation channels 13 cm dia at r = 102.1 cm, height 450 cm
  KLAK 6 cm upper/lower, 88.2743 cm2 middle; hot gas duct D=30 cm L=100 cm
  Pebble packing fraction 0.61; upper-surface cone angle 19.5 deg

Also independently confirms packing fraction 0.61 for op-5c5r, and gives the 19.5 deg cone angle -- but Terry says that angle was CALCULATED by an INL DEM code and explicitly NOT measured, so it is a modelling assumption, not data.

STILL OPEN: the 83-zone R-Z boundaries of TECDOC Table 4-3 are NOT in this paper. Terry section 1 says it is a summary and directs the reader to the IRPhEP evaluation report itself (its ref [3]) for the detailed benchmark model. Obtaining THAT report is the remaining work here. Recommend keeping this bead open at P2 and retitling scope to the zone boundaries only.

Facts vs document: the numbers are recorded because facts are not copyrightable and Terry section 1 states all descriptive data came from published documents, mainly the two IAEA TECDOCs which this workspace already holds OPEN -- so they have an open provenance path. For publication, cite the IRPhEP report or the TECDOCs, NOT this preprint.

notes.author: fifad@Teddy-Thinkpad
notes.content:
CORRECTION 2026-08-13, superseding my previous comment on this bead. I claimed Terry does not contain the R-Z zone boundaries. That was WRONG. It was concluded from the extracted TEXT only (130 lines), which genuinely lacks them -- but the paper's FIGURES carry them: section 2 describes Fig. 2 as the simplified model, 'axisymmetric (the borings are homogenized in the zones where they are located)', which is exactly the R-Z zone map. Fig. 1 is the high-fidelity version.

They are RASTER: the PDF has 5 /Subtype /Image objects, all FlateDecode, and zero vector drawing operators, so coordinates are not exactly recoverable from the content stream. The figures must be DIGITISED with kovan-digitise (CLI, per the CLAUDE.md hard rule -- never read points off a figure by eye; only the maintainer may mark a dataset reviewed).

USEFUL SYNERGY: an engineering figure has no axes to calibrate against, but Terry's Table 2 gives exact known dimensions -- core radius 90 cm, reflector OD 380 cm, reflector height 610 cm -- which serve as explicit --x-ref/--y-ref pixel=value anchors. Table 2 sets the scale, Fig. 2 gives the boundaries.

BLOCKED ON TOOLING: kovan lit import cannot emit the figures. extract_assets() exists in the library (pdf_import.rs:70) but the CLI has no flag for it. Filed as its own bead.

ALSO STILL WORTH OBTAINING: ref [3], 'International Handbook of Evaluated Reactor Physics Benchmark Experiments', NEA/NSC/DOC(2006)1, OECD NEA (2006) -- Terry section 1 directs the reader there for the full benchmark model. Tabulated boundaries would beat digitised ones.

design:
Part of the dwsim-libs maturity epic (bn op-otqe).

Add a dated maturity declaration to
`crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs/CLAUDE.md`, following the format the gate
(#58) established: date, validation/reference basis, evidence class, known
limitations, and API dogfood status.

## Declare four axes separately

These have genuinely different evidence levels and collapsing them into one bar
would overstate the crate:

| # | axis | current evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | thermodynamic / property package | to be established — see validation sub-issue |
| 2 | rigorous MESH numerical solver | 682 `#[test]` markers; needs a published benchmark |
| 3 | crude pseudo-component characterization | to be established against a documented assay |
| 4 | **refinery-unit-model fidelity** | **weakest — see below** |

## Preserve the existing honesty on axis 4

The crate already documents its own limits well, and this **must not be
softened**:

> Atmospheric column only — no vacuum tower, no pre-flash, no crude furnace,
> no pump-arounds, and no steam stripping. It is a teaching and scoping model
> in the same spirit as the benzene column, not a refinery simulator.

> **A real CDU is not reboiled.** It is a refluxed absorber stripped with open
> steam at the bottom, with pump-around circuits removing heat down the column.

**Do not silently relabel this model as a refinery-grade CDU.** The converged
cut slate in the epic demonstrates the execution path works; it says nothing
about predictive accuracy against a real crude unit.

## An actionable detail found while filing

`ColumnType::RefluxedAbsorber` **already exists in the solver's enum**.
`RigorousColumn::distillation` is the only constructor and fixes the type to a
reboiled distillation column, so the other variant is unreachable — reaching it
means extending that builder.

This is the exact pattern #58 kept finding: **the data model exists, the access
seam is missing.** It means the distance to a structurally correct CDU is a
constructor plus steam/pump-around handling, not new solver physics. Worth
stating in the declaration so the limitation reads as bounded work rather than
a fundamental gap.

## Also

Record **API dogfood status** as a field — the #58 declarations predate this
programme and do not carry one. Backfilling it for the other declared crates is
worth doing in the same pass.
title: dwsim-libs: maturity declaration across four fidelity axes

description:
FIXED 2026-08-13. RE-FILED after tracker data loss (see docs/kopitiam-issues/).

The op-ad6h defect existed in THREE places: outram-foam-basic-lib, tampines-steam-tables/src/openfoam_algorithms/openfoam_source/ode/, and outram-park-fork-coolprop/src/openfoam_algorithms/openfoam_source/. diff -r showed the two vendored trees differ only in doc wording and use-ordering.

Confirmed by demonstration, not inference. In BOTH trees Rosenbrock23::solve_step imports integrate_interval and normalize_error but NOT adaptive_step, so it duplicates the retry loop; the guard was proven load-bearing by deleting it and watching the tests fail with Err(StepSizeUnderflow) instead of Err(NonFiniteState).

SEVERITY NUANCE: the enum variant surfaced NO consumers in either crate -- OdeError appears only inside openfoam_source/ode/, and adaptive_step is called only by euler.rs and rkf45.rs. So here the defect was LATENT, a trap for the first consumer, unlike basic-lib where it was actively reachable.

Gates: tampines-steam-tables 955 passed / 0 failed / 13 ignored; outram-park-fork-coolprop 282 / 0 / 4; cargo check --workspace --lib --release clean.

RECOMMENDATION for op-xji, not acted on: delete both vendored ODE sub-trees and depend on outram-foam-basic-lib. One defect fixed three times is the concrete case op-xji describes, and the ODE sub-tree is the cheapest pilot because it has ZERO consumers -- removing it changes no behaviour and no public surface. Countervailing constraint documented in coolprop openfoam_algorithms/CLAUDE.md: the vendoring is deliberate so that crate depends only on uom and stays Android-buildable, whereas basic-lib pulls ndarray. Maintainer decision.
